reasoning_traces.think:
The core mathematical structure of the injury prediction framework is a stochastic process defined over time-varying biomechanical inputs. The injury risk model R(t) is formulated as a composite of load history and temporal strain, both derived from physical measurements. The load kernel K(t) is a convolution of force and velocity, representing mechanical stress accumulation. The temporal strain index S(t) tracks fatigue through an exponential moving average of physiological indicators. These primitives form a dual system: one deterministic (load kernel) and one probabilistic (risk model). Failure modes include sensor drift, non-stationarity of athlete behavior, and insufficient calibration data. The system assumes ergodicity of training load and independence of injury events, which may not hold under high-intensity or novel movement patterns.
